root_idea.summary: The root centers on the intermixture or entanglement of things with one another, especially when gathered into a single grasp.
root_idea.development: The physical image of separate stalks or herbs collected into a handful extends figuratively to confused dreams, reports, affairs, and speech.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular noun citation form ضِغْثٌ; the Quran occurrences include both this singular form and its plural أَضْغَاثٌ.

senses.definition: A handful or bundle of gathered plant matter—such as herbage, twigs, or stalks—grasped together.
senses.usage_conditions: In ضِغْثًا in 38:44, it denotes a concrete bundle taken in the hand.

senses.definition: A confused medley of dreams, whose elements are mixed so that their truth or interpretation is not clear.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the plural expression أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ in 12:44 and 21:5 for incoherent or muddled dreams.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect a thing or things together.
To confuse or relate a tradition, story, or similar discourse in a confused manner.
To wash a garment without fully cleansing it, leaving it in an uncleansed or dubious state.
To feel a camel’s hump to determine whether it is fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be the hump itself or the she-camel being examined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make plants or herbage into bunches or bundles.
To pour water onto the head and divide or rub the hair into separate handfuls while washing it.
To collect a handful of herbage in which fresh and dry material are mixed.
The state of a thing’s parts being confused or mixed with one another.
A confused or mixed assortment, especially of news; by extension, a mixed or insincere deed or speech lacking good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically applied to assorted reports, a confused affair, a deed lacking purity, and speech in which there is no good.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or bundle of worldly goods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage attested in traditional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose fatness is uncertain and whose hump is felt to assess it; also, such a doubtful camel’s hump.
Rain that moistens the earth and herbage.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The reported cry-related sense is explicitly corrected in the passage to the spelling ضَغَبَ.
The entry reports a fright-related sense but explicitly says the word is correctly ضَاغِبٌ with ب.

cautions: The Quranic noun has two distinct attested uses here: the singular concrete bundle in 38:44 and the plural dream-medley expression in 12:44 and 21:5.
The modern verse locations shown are supplied QAC locations; historical Lane citation notation was not used to derive them.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:Dgv:17824:g3:main and lane-unit:Dgv:17832:g1:main preserve disputed cry-related entries under ضغث/ضاغث, but their own discussion corrects the spelling to ضغب/ضاغب, so they are not confidently assigned to this root.
